Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG packet last week. Our security team reviewed the encryption controls section and has two follow-ups we need to close before the next procurement milestone:

- Clarify key rotation cadence for customer data keys and the root/wrapping keys (schedule + evidence).
- Provide proof of rotation events (key IDs, timestamps) and the corresponding audit trail export (CloudTrail or equivalent).
- Confirm whether the root/wrapping keys are under HSM custody (CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) and, if so, provide FIPS/FedRAMP attestation details for the HSM environment.

We attached an excerpt of the SIG PDF with the specific questions highlighted. Can you point us to the rotation records and let us know the expected delivery timing? We prefer a secure upload link for artifacts. If it helps, we can do a 30-minute sync.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our legal procurement deadline is end of next week.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez

Parhelion Technologies

Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on encryption / KMS rotation items — rotation details & exports

Marta / team — attaching the first export and a short summary here. Quick summary of our encryption posture: 

- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (prefer 1.3) with strong cipher suites; mutual TLS supported for Private deployments.
- At rest: customer data encrypted with AES-256-GCM using envelope encryption. Data keys are generated and stored in AWS KMS (primary), with optional Azure Key Vault for customers in that cloud.
- Root/wrapping keys: stored in FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs (AWS CloudHSM clusters) for Redwood-managed keys. For customers using BYOK, we support customer HSMs or EKM integrations.

Rotation policy and evidence: 
- Data keys (DEKs) are rotated automatically per-customer on a 30-day sliding schedule by default; we rotate the envelope DEK and rewrap with the current KMS Customer Master Key (CMK).
- CMKs (wrapping keys) are rotated annually by default. For high-security customers we support a 90-day or on-demand rotation cadence via a configuration flag.
- Rotation events are logged in CloudTrail with the KMS API calls (ScheduleKeyDeletion, RotateKey, ReEncrypt, GenerateDataKey) and recorded in our E2E audit index.

Attached: kms-rotation-ops-202611-entries.csv — columns: key_id, key_alias, event_type, event_ts, region, initiating_principal. This is an export of rotation-related KMS events between 2026-10-01 and 2026-11-20.

HSM attestation: AWS CloudHSM is FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 (per cluster config); Neha is preparing vendor attestation PDFs that list the FIPS statements and our configuration.

Notes on evidence delivery:
- We will provide a CloudTrail export slice for the key events (JSON) and an index CSV.
- We can redact internal-only principals if you need a vendor-facing artifact.

If any of the specific fields in the SIG require different formats, let us know and we will adapt. I will upload the CSV and the preliminary zip package to a secure location and paste the link here shortly.

Attachment: kms-rotation-ops-202611-entries.csv (CSV, 48KB)

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@parhelion.com>

Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on encryption / KMS rotation items — rotation details & exports

Thanks Vivek — that summary helps. A couple of asks to close the outstanding SIG questions: 

1) Can you provide the CloudTrail export (or equivalent) that shows the KMS RotateKey / ReEncrypt events for the CMK over the last 12 months? We need timestamps, key IDs, and the initiating principal.
2) Please include the HSM vendor attestation and the cluster configuration that demonstrates FIPS compliance.
3) For the BYOK flows, describe whether Redwood stores any copy of the customer master key material, and provide the key escrow/backup policy if applicable.

If possible we'd like these artifacts in a signed ZIP (checksum + timestamp) via a secure upload. Can you also confirm whether the CMK rotation is an AWS-native automatic rotation (enabled=true) or a Redwood-managed rotation script (we saw both in different customers)?

If it's easier, we can take a 30-minute call today to walk through the artifacts. Are you available at 16:00 PST?

Best,
Marta
